questions.question: In which of the following part of Neuron the information is transmitted in the chemical form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No option is correct**__.

__
 
• At **synapses **of the Neuron, the information is transmitted in the chemical form, called as **Neurotransmitter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Synapse:

 
 
• It is the junction between 2 neurons.
 
• There is a very narrow gap of about 20nm between neurons called the synaptic cleft.
 
• An action potential cannot cross the synaptic cleft, so nerve impulses are carried by chemicals called neurotransmitters.
 
 
 
• The structure of a synapse:
 
 
• At the synapse, the presynaptic neuron communicates with the postsynaptic neuron.
 
• At the end of the presynaptic neuron, there are synaptic knobs.
 
• Synaptic knobs contain many mitochondria and large amounts of ER to manufacture neurotransmitters.
 
• There is a tiny gap known as the synaptic cleft
 
 
 
• Functions of a synapse:
 
 
• A single impulse is transmitted to a number of different neurons creating simultaneous responses.
 
• A number of impulses are combined at a synapse allowing stimuli from different receptors to interact for a single response.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support?
questions.solution: Epithelial tissue forms a lining all over the body of the organism in order to protect the inner lying parts. They act as a barrier that keep the different body systems separate. Cuboidal epithelial tissue forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support.

questions.question: Which part of the human body has the growth stages divided into - Anagen, Catagen and Telogen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Hair__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human body's hair follicles comprise three distinctive phases: **anagen, catagen, and telogen phase**.
 
• **Anagen** is the growth phase and approximately 85% of all hairs are in a growing phase at any one time.
 
• **Melanin** is made in the hair bulb throughout this phase. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__**
 
• The** catagen** phase follows the anagen stage it is a **1- to 2-week transition stage between anagen and telogen**.
 
• **The telogen phase **is referred to as the resting phase which typically lasts for 3 months.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue allows transportation of substances through a selective permeable surface in the lining of food vessels or lung alveoli?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simple squamous epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Simple squamous epithelium:

 
 
• ​It is a single layer of flat-scale-shaped cells.
 
• This tissue makes up the inner lining of the mouth and blood vessels.
 
• It also makes the mesothelial lining of the body cavities.
 
• It allows the transportation of substances through a selective permeable surface in the lining of food vessels or lung alveoli.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5624e9915657362a75a5b4016fe458359e40fb0ef265856efb3ec8773aee89f9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ciliated columnar epithelium tissues are found in the fallopian tube and parts of the respiratory system.
 
• Stratified squamous epithelium tissues are found in the organ system where the body comes into close contact with the outside environment 
 
• Columnar epithelium tissues are found in the stomach and intestines.

questions.question: The Atrial wall of the human heart secretes a very important peptide hormone. What is the name of that hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ANF.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (** ANP **) is also known as Atrial Natriuretic Factor (** ANF** ).
 
• It is a type of hormone that is secreted from the cardiac atria. 
 
• The function of ANP includes causing a reduction in expanded** extracellular fluid ( ECF )** volume by increasing renal sodium excretion.
 
• ANP is synthesized and secreted by cardiac muscle cells in the walls of atria in the heart.
 
• **Volume receptors** are present in these cells that respond to increased stretching of the arterial wall due to increased atrial blood volume.
 
• **De Bold in 1981** discovered the natriuretic factor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The gastric inhibitory polypeptide, a hormone secreted by cells of the** intestinal mucosa that blocks the secretion of hydrochloric acid into the stomach.**
 
• Cholecystokinin (CCK) is a neuropeptide and gut hormone that r**egulates pancreatic enzyme secretion and gastrointestinal motility and acts as a satiety signal.**
 
• ADH is also called arginine vasopressin, a hormone made **by the hypothalamus in the brain** and stored in the posterior pituitary gland. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**There are a total of three types of atrial natriuretic peptide receptors namely** -

 
• NPR1
 
• NPR2
 
• NPR3

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the function(s) of bile juice released from the liver?

I. Make the food coming from stomach alkaline.

II. Conversion of proteins into amino acids.

III. Break down of fats into smaller globules.
questions.solution:
Bile makes the food coming from the stomach alkaline.

Break down fats into smaller globules.

__**EXPLANATION:**__

 
• The liver secretes bile. When bile leaves the liver, it gets stored in the gallbladder, before being released into the duodenum.
 
• When it gets released from the gallbladder, it breaks large fat globules into smaller particles. This is known as emulsification.
 
• As Bile is alkaline in nature, it neutralizes acidic food coming from the stomach to provide the alkaline conditions needed in the small intestine.

questions.question: The right pulmonary artery is ______.

options.text: of same size as the left

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __longer than the left__.**

 
• The** right pulmonary artery **is the** longer of the two**.
 
• It passes transversely across the midline in the upper chest and passes below the aortic arch to enter the hilum of the right lung as part of its root.
 
• The** left pulmonary artery **is the** shorter **of the two terminal branches of the pulmonary trunk.
 
• It pierces the pericardium (the sac around the heart) and enters the hilum of the left lung.
 
• These arteries then deliver **oxygen-depleted blood **to each corresponding lung.
 
• This is one of the rare arteries that carry deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: Which of the following is a trace mineral in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Selenium__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **trace mineral**

 
 
• A **trace element/minor element**; is a chemical element whose concentration is very low.
 
• These include **iron, manganese, copper, iodine, zinc, cobalt, fluoride and selenium**.
 
• These minerals are present in** living tissues **of human body in small amounts.
 
• Some of them are known to be **nutritionally essential, others may be essential and the remainder are considered to be nonessential**.
 
 
 
• **Selenium**
 
 
• **Jons Jacob Berzelius** discovered the Selenium.
 
• Selenium bellongs to group **16 of periodic table**.
 
• It belongs to the** P- block **of periodic tabe.

questions.question: Scientists of which country have developed working human skeletal muscle from stem cells in the laboratory for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**United States of America.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Scientists from Duke University, North Carolina, USA have developed working human skeletal muscle from stem cells in the laboratory for the first time.
 
• The human skeletal muscle was developed using blood cells or adult skin reprogrammed into a versatile and juvenile state.
 
• This development might help those who suffer from degenerative muscular diseases.
